requirement: S3B §6.1 / §15.8: the invocation ledger must account for every model call, and every committed event must trace to one
gate_completeness_rule: complete = no pending and no failed; uncommitted expert decisions are normal by construction, because the decision stage emits no event (§6.1)

observation.what: one REPORT call (case-37, call-case-37-00042) parsed as accepted but committed no event, while call-case-37-00070 committed the case's single FINAL_REPORT event
observation.why_it_matters: the event stream shows one report; the ledger shows two report calls. This is the S3A dual-channel argument visible in real data: the event stream alone cannot distinguish 'the model was asked once' from 'asked, and the first answer was discarded without a trace'.
observation.cause: not determined from the artifacts; the call sits between a belief-graph update and the next CENTRAL_PLAN, consistent with a report generated speculatively mid-loop and only emitted when the run actually stops
observation.impact_on_s3b: none on eligibility: the gate's completeness rule counts pending and failed calls, and both are 0 for every case. Reported so the count is not read as an unexplained gap.

note: 'unbound commit' -- a commit that matched no call -- is the defect S3A added _unbound_commits to catch. It is 0 here.
